# Link adaptation


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A PHY abstraction with several rates (e.g. the MCSs of a table) rates
each transmission at every one of them.
[`LinkAdaptation`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/link_adaptation.html#linkadaptation)
then picks one per transmission: the fastest whose error rate meets a
target, or the slowest if none does. The copies of a broadcast get one
rate, the fastest meeting the target at every receiver: the weakest
receiver’s.
[`SionnaErrorModel`](https://Ahmed-Khaled-Saleh.github.io/comm-core/sionna_sys.html#sionnaerrormodel)
uses it (see `sionna_sys`); it works on numpy arrays and torch tensors.

It is the rule of Sionna SYS’s `InnerLoopLinkAdaptation`
(`sionna.sys.link_adaptation`), which also has an outer loop correcting
the SINR from acknowledgements (OLLA); one would go here.

### LinkAdaptation

``` python
class LinkAdaptation(
    target:float=0.1, # The highest error rate allowed
):
```

*The fastest rate meeting a target error rate (else the slowest): one
per transmission, one for all the copies of a broadcast.*

### LinkAdaptation.call

``` python
def call(
    error_rate, # Error rate of each transmission at each rate, (n, M), the rates from slowest to fastest (numpy or torch)
    group:Sequence | None=None, # The broadcast of each transmission, None for a unicast (None: all unicasts)
):
```

*Index of the rate chosen for each transmission, (n,).*

``` python
rates = np.array([[0.0, 0.05, 0.5], [0.0, 0.2, 0.9], [0.5, 0.9, 1.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.01]])
la = LinkAdaptation(target=0.1)
assert la(rates).tolist() == [1, 0, 0, 2]                                 # none meets it (row 2): the slowest
assert la(rates, group=['x', 'x', None, 'y']).tolist() == [0, 0, 0, 2]     # a broadcast: its weakest receiver's
```
